findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the durability edit to add peer_confirmations.json (its git_adapter FILE constant) to BOTH `_rel_files` AND the `_tracked_basenames` set in `_commit_binding_store_snapshot`, and cover a peer-confirmation-only-change commit in AC7.
evidence: Plan: 'add the new file to the staged `_rel_files` list in `reconcile_helpers.py::_commit_binding_store_snapshot`'
reconcile_helpers.py line 234-240 builds a SEPARATE `_tracked_basenames` set and gates the commit on `if not (_tracked_basenames & _staged_basenames): return True  # Already up-to-date`
The bug-1e08 comment (lines 226-230) explains this per-basename guard exists precisely so a single-file-only change is not skipped
findings.finding: The durability edit under-specifies the second file guard in _commit_binding_store_snapshot: adding peer_confirmations.json to _rel_files alone leaves it out of the _tracked_basenames set (the bug-1e08 per-file idempotency check), so a peer-confirmation-only staged change hits `_tracked_basenames & _staged_basenames` == empty and returns 'nothing to commit', silently dropping the store — the exact b8b1 loss the plan cites.
scenarios: A pass records a peer confirmation but touches no other binding-state file: _rel_files stages peer_confirmations.json, but _tracked_basenames does not contain it, so the intersection is empty and the commit is skipped — the record is lost on the next checkout
findings.suggested_fix: Amend the Durability bullet to name both the `_rel_files` list (line 207) and the `_tracked_basenames` set (lines 234-238), plus a new `git_adapter.PEER_CONFIRMATIONS_FILE` constant; AC7 should assert the file both appears staged AND actually commits when it is the only changed file.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the 'no key translation is needed' claim: specify that the write site reverse-maps to_key→target_local_id via binding_store.get_local_id and takes source_local_id from mutation['local_id'], and thread a binding_store into _update_one_dispatch_links / update_one so the (source_local_id, target_local_id, relation) key matches the S3 reader.
evidence: outbound_links.py:101-110 emits {action:add, type, to_key, relation, swap, link_uuid} — to_key is the target JIRA KEY, not a local id
dispatch_one.py:654 `_update_one_dispatch_links(mutation, client, issue_key)` — issue_key is the source JIRA KEY; no binding_store parameter
apply_inbound_records.py:546 `_inbound_unlink_one(local_id, target_local_id, relation, ...)` — the named S3 reader keys on LOCAL ids
binding_store.py:324 `get_local_id(jira_key)` exists as the reverse map; outbound_links.py:159 already uses it for the opposite direction
mutation.get('local_id') supplies the SOURCE local id (create_one reads it), but no field supplies the TARGET local id
findings.finding: The plan asserts 'no key translation is needed' at the write site, but the record key (source_local_id, target_local_id, relation) needs LOCAL ids while the outbound ADD entry carries only Jira keys (issue_key as source, entry['to_key'] as target); the target local id requires a binding_store.get_local_id(to_key) reverse-map, and _update_one_dispatch_links (and update_one) receive no binding_store today.
findings.location: Scope → 'Write site' bullet ('The outbound ADD payload already carries relation, so no key translation is needed'); AC3
scenarios: Store is keyed by Jira keys → S3's local-id lookup never matches → every managed link reads as 'not confirmed', silently defeating the store's purpose
Store is keyed by local ids but the write site has no binding_store → the target local id cannot be resolved and the record cannot be written
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the binding_store through update_one to _update_one_dispatch_links; build the key as (mutation['local_id'], binding_store.get_local_id(entry['to_key']), entry['relation']); when the target reverse-map returns None, skip recording (unbound target, retry next pass) rather than writing a Jira-key-shaped key.

scenarios: reconcile_helpers.py:234 `_tracked_basenames` set — if peer_confirmations.json's basename is not added here, a pass in which ONLY peer_confirmations.json changed fails the `_tracked_basenames & _staged_basenames` check at line 240 and returns 'nothing to commit', silently dropping the store (documented bug 1e08 failure mode).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Disambiguate the two `source` uses: rename the positional local-id params (e.g. `source_local_id`/`target_local_id`) or rename the provenance field, so one identifier does not name both.
evidence: API: `is_confirmed(source, target, relation)`
Record fields: `source` (`push` | `snapshot` | `backfill`)
the record() param that sets this field is named `source_kind`, but the positional is `source`
findings.finding: The identifier `source` is used with two different meanings in the API surface: as a positional parameter naming the source_local_id (`is_confirmed(source, target, relation)`, `record(source, target, relation, ...)`) AND as a record field naming provenance (`source` = `push`|`snapshot`|`backfill`). This collision can confuse the implementer about which `source` a call site means.
scenarios: Implementer writes record() and confuses the positional source (local id) with the provenance source field
findings.suggested_fix: Use `source_local_id`/`target_local_id` for the key params and keep the provenance field as `source` (populated by `source_kind`), or rename the field to `provenance`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the RETIRE/cleanup lifecycle for peer_confirmations records (who prunes them and when, or an explicit note that pruning is owned by a named later story) so the store does not leak unbounded.
evidence: Lifecycle CREATE (record) and CONSUME (is_confirmed) are defined; no RETIRE path is mentioned
AC5 confirms round-trip survival across compaction but nothing prunes obsolete records
Out of scope defers S3 removal but does not assign the confirmation-record cleanup
findings.finding: The store accumulates a record per managed link with no described RETIRE/cleanup path. When a link is legitimately removed (or its ticket deleted/compacted away), the confirmation record persists indefinitely, so the sidecar grows unbounded and can hold stale confirmations for links that no longer exist.
scenarios: A managed link is removed downstream; its peer_confirmations record is never pruned
Store grows monotonically over many passes
findings.suggested_fix: Add a Scope note: either a record-pruning hook (e.g. drop on confirmed removal) or an explicit deferral to S3/S4 with the owning story id and rationale for why unbounded growth is acceptable until then.
